name: What is included in a full-service pool removal estimate?

mainEntity.name: What should a full-service in-ground pool removal estimate include so there are no surprise charges?
mainEntity.text: What should a full-service in-ground pool removal estimate include so there are no surprise charges?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong estimate should be itemized, not just a single lump sum. At minimum, it should state whether the contractor is pricing partial or full removal, how debris will be hauled, who handles permits, and whether compaction and final grading are included. It should also clarify restoration items like irrigation repair, concrete patching, fencing, and landscape cleanup. The biggest problem with vague pool removal bids is that they hide exclusions that become change orders later. Homeowners in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, and nearby cities should also ask about access fees, protection of existing hardscape, and disposal costs because those can vary a lot by property. A complete estimate makes it easier to compare contractors fairly and helps avoid disputes after the work starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A good estimate should list demolition, debris haul-off, permit handling, utility disconnects, backfill, compaction, grading, cleanup, and any restoration of hardscape or landscaping. It should also state what is excluded, such as engineering, drainage work, tree protection, or export fees. Vague bids often lead to change orders later.
